_note: V02 - Core/Stream inline call surfaces (architecture/proposals/inline-native-surfaces.md), judged against the SAME law stripe.json pins: the module owns the session and the overlay face (dsx.module.stream.open, the vendor's full-screen call UI) and the component face (<stream.CallView/> and friends) are two views onto ONE state machine. Two call models that disagree is a participant who left the call on one face and is still publishing on the other, so a second join attempt while one is in flight is refused `busy` and every outcome reaches both faces including one that unmounted mid-join. gate[] is the LIVE SURFACE LADDER: a call tile needs camera and microphone before it can render anything, and a permission nobody has asked for yet renders the ASK, never the refusal. roster[] is the tile ORDER: deterministic on three renderers, because a grid that re-sorts under a finger is the complaint every call app gets first, and the local participant sinks below the person talking.

sessionRef._note: The security boundary for <stream.CallView/> session=. A Stream call is entered with a USER TOKEN, which is a JWT, and the corpus pins what happens when one is pasted into markup: it is REFUSED. Note WHICH refusal - `unknown_reference`, not `literal_secret`, because the credential families the shared detector knows are Stripe's. The allowlist is what refuses it, which is exactly why the rule is an allowlist and not a denylist of key prefixes.

cases._note: The row above uses a truncated signature, so it lands on unknown_reference: a segment under 8 characters is not a JWT, and guessing would let any dotted string be reported as a leaked credential. A real token has three segments of real length, and naming the family is what turns the message from "that is not a reference" into "you pasted a token".

machine._note: One call, two views. `start` is the JOIN attempt, `complete` is connected, `fail` is a join that did not land and leaves the call re-joinable (NOT terminal - a network blip must not strand a user on a dead screen), `cancel` while joining backs out of the attempt and keeps the call, and `cancel` with nothing in flight LEAVES the call, which is terminal.

THE DOUBLE-JOIN GUARD: the other face cannot start a second join
a failed join is retryable: the call is still there
the tile unmounts mid-join and is STILL told the outcome
detaching a tile never ends the call

leaving is terminal, and a second leave is refused
a tile that never attached cannot join
joining before the module has a call is not_ready

CLOSING MID-JOIN TAKES TWO CANCELS: back out of the attempt, then leave the call. The first cancel returns confirming->ready, which is NOT terminal - a module that stops there leaves the vendor call running off screen, billing (S1 BUG-1).

CLOSING A CONNECTED CALL: the machine is already terminal and REFUSES the cancel. That refusal is bookkeeping about the ATTEMPT, never a reason to keep a WebRTC session alive - the module leaves the vendor call first and reads this refusal as `already over`.
a failed join closes in ONE cancel: `failed` is not settled, so the session leaves directly

NOTHING BUT A SETTLE OR A CANCEL LEAVES CONFIRMING. Attaching and detaching a second face while a join is in flight moves nothing, which is why `settle` has to be invoked from a real connection transition and cannot be left to a component lifecycle (S1 BUG-1's other half).
the overlay face joined and the INLINE face closes: ONE call, ONE leave, and both faces are told

gate._note: The live-surface ladder every camera or microphone component descends before it renders. ORDER IS THE LAW: capability first, because a device with no camera must not be asked for camera permission and an unlinked SDK cannot answer a permission word. Then the permission, where `prompt` and `unknown` both render the ASK: a surface that fails closed on a not-yet-asked permission never gets asked.

roster._note: Tile order for a call grid. Tiers, most important first: pinned, screen share, dominant speaker, other remotes, then LOCAL last - a user looking at their own face instead of the person talking is the first thing anyone reports. Ties break on join time and then on id, so the same roster is the same grid on three renderers and an unrelated re-render does not shuffle tiles under a finger. columns[] is hardcoded on all three renderers on purpose.

retain._note: Keyed identity for an expensive vendor view (the SceneBind law). A call tile holds a live WebRTC track: tearing it down on an unrelated re-render drops video for a second and costs a renegotiation, so identity is declared and never positional-by-accident.

connection._note: THE CONNECTION FOLD. `dsx.module.stream.context.connection` is one six-word vocabulary (offline / connecting / connected / reconnecting / migrating / failed) that a `reconnecting` banner is markup against, and `settle` is what escapes the session machine's `confirming` - so this fold is simultaneously the reactive var and the ONLY thing allowed to invoke `settle`. S1 assumed both native SDKs already spoke one `RealtimeConnection` vocabulary. THEY DO NOT: stream-video-android-core has `RealtimeConnection` (PreJoin/InProgress/Joined/Connected/Reconnecting/Migrating/Failed/ReconnectingFailed/Disconnected), @stream-io/video-client has a `CallingState` enum (unknown/idle/ringing/joining/joined/left/reconnecting/migrating/reconnecting-failed/offline), and stream-video-swift has NEITHER - it has `CallingState` (idle/lobby/incoming/outgoing/joining/inCall/reconnecting) plus a separate `ReconnectionStatus` (connected/reconnecting/migrating/disconnected) that the module folds in first. There IS a translation table, so it is pinned here rather than trusted. Note the collision the lane key exists for: the word `joined` means CONNECTED on web and still-connecting on Android (the SDK's own comment: `joined, participant state is available, video isn't ready yet`). An unknown word on any lane is offline with NO settle: a fold that cannot read the SDK must never invent a connected call.

renderer._note: THE TILE FOLD - what <stream.ParticipantTile/> publishes and WHICH track it binds. V02 shipped the tile's chrome over an empty `StreamInlineHandles.renderer` seam and published `video:false` on every platform; this section is that seam's contract, so the three renderers cannot disagree about which track a tile is holding. It deliberately pins the DECISION and not the platform plumbing (VideoRendererView.handleViewRendering on iOS, StreamVideoTextureViewRenderer + Call.initRenderer on Android, call.bindVideoElement on web), exactly as net/status.json pins the classification and not NWPathMonitor. THE KEYED-RETAIN LAW'S COMPANION: `track` is what the retain key must be re-bound against, because a tile that keeps its live renderer across a reorder while its participant changed underneath is a tile showing the wrong person's face. A shared screen is NEVER mirrored and a remote participant is never mirrored, whatever mirror= says: mirroring is a fact about your own camera.
